title: Kummer cup-product basis for a strictly local normal crossings complement
statement:
Let $R$ be a Noetherian strictly henselian regular local ring, $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$, and $\ell$ a prime invertible in $R$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology, def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $\mathfrak m$ be the maximal ideal of $R$ and let $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in\mathfrak m$ have linearly independent images in the residue-field vector space $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ and put $V=D(f_1\cdots f_r)\subseteq T$ [def-weil-open-immersion]. The empty list is allowed and gives $V=T$. There exists $\zeta\in R^\times$ with $\zeta^\ell=1$ and $1-\zeta^a\in R^\times$ for $1\leq a<\ell$; for any such choice identify the roots-of-unity sheaf $\mu_\ell$ with $\underline{\mathbf F_\ell}$ by $a\mapsto\zeta^a$ [def-asd-etale-roots-of-unity, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Write $\kappa_\zeta(f_i)\in H^1(V,\underline{\mathbf F_\ell})$ for the class of the torsor $t^\ell=f_i$ under this identification, equivalently its Kummer connecting class [lem-amb-kummer-any-base]. On the ordinary small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], for every $q\geq0$ the classes
$$\kappa_\zeta(f_{i_1})\smile\cdots\smile\kappa_\zeta(f_{i_q})\qquad(1\leq i_1<\cdots<i_q\leq r)$$
form an $\mathbf F_\ell$-basis of $H^q(V,\underline{\mathbf F_\ell})$. For $q=0$ this means the basis $1$; for $q>r$ the group is zero. Cup product means the cohomology pairing induced by multiplication of the constant coefficient ring. For any local homomorphism $R\to R'$ to a Noetherian strictly henselian regular local ring for which the images of $f_i$ have linearly independent classes in $\mathfrak m_{R'}/\mathfrak m_{R'}^2$, canonical pullback sends each displayed product to the product of the Kummer classes of the images of the same $f_i$, with the image of $\zeta$ as coefficient identification.

source.place: Expose XV Theorem 2.1.2 and proof of Proposition 2.1.7, printed pp.220–221; Expose XVI Corollary 3.1.3 and its proof, printed pp.242–243. The chosen-root formulation spells out the branch generators and their functoriality. The cotangent-space formulation is XV Definition 2.1.4 and consequence 2.1.5; existence of the coefficient identification is the strictly henselian case of the etale roots-of-unity sheaf.
